headline: Sheinbaum picks Beijing over Madrid
body:
Mexico's president confirmed she'll attend the APEC Leaders' Summit in Shenzhen, China (Nov 18-19) — while casting doubt on the Iberoamerican Summit in Madrid that same month.

The signal is unmistakable: when forced to choose between Asia and Europe, Mexico's calendar tilts toward the Pacific. Trade diversification isn't rhetoric anymore — it's flight bookings.

Sovereignty means choosing your own meetings.

headline: EU-Mexico trade deal signing: May 22
body:
Sheinbaum and European Council President Costa confirmed the 8th EU-Mexico Summit in Mexico City on May 22. They'll sign the Modernized Global Agreement — a decade in the making.

The deal eliminates tariffs on 86% of agricultural goods immediately. US producers are already sounding alarms about losing market share in Mexico.

Washington spent years telling Mexico "diversify" was a threat. Turns out it's a strategy — and the EU just RSVP'd.

headline: Sheinbaum's steel plan: sovereignty, not submission
body:
Mexico's new steel policy will cut imports from China and South Korea — but not because Washington said so.

The goal: protect Mexican steelmakers and build domestic industrial capacity. This isn't Trump's tariff playbook. It's industrial policy with a national interest compass.

Mexico reduces Chinese steel dependency on its own terms, for its own reasons. That's the difference between sovereignty and obedience.

headline: The China-Mexico FDI paradox
body:
Chinese FDI announcements in Mexico dropped 80% in 2025 (from $3B to $588M). Nearshoring announcements fell 78% in Q1 2026.

But here's the twist: completed Chinese projects in Q1 2026 hit $4.95 billion — investments committed before the pressure campaign kicked in.

The pipeline is real. The question is whether US pressure and USMCA uncertainty will choke the next wave — or just push it underground.

Multipolar supply chains don't disappear. They adapt.

headline: Puente Nichupté: "Where there was corruption, today there is honesty"
body:
Sheinbaum inaugurated the Nichupté bridge in Cancún — 11.2 km, cutting commute from 1 hour to 10 minutes.

Tribute to Mexican workers on May Day weekend. "Tiempo de vida" — this is what infrastructure means when it serves the people, not the contractors.

headline: Beca Gertrudis Bocanegra: "Sovereignty emanates from the people"
body:
In Palenque, Chiapas — 56,911 students receiving scholarships. Leona Vicario quoted on women fighting for the nation.

"La técnica al servicio de la patria" — 23 million students supported across all programs. IPN campus growth continuing.

headline: "Under no circumstances will we allow interference of a foreign government"
body:
Sheinbaum on US extradition requests for Mexican officials including the governor of Sinaloa:

"What evidence do they have? Witnesses whose identities we don't know."
"If clear evidence does not exist, the objective is political."
"A US ambassador cannot have an interventionist attitude."

Children's Day: "We want girls and boys to be happy. They have special rights." Education: 15.2M Beca Rita Cetina recipients, 99% school enrollment.

headline: Trump: "We will take Cuba almost immediately" — Díaz-Canel: "Fear doesn't eat here"
body: Trump escalates rhetoric on Cuba while Díaz-Canel responds with defiance. Latin America watches as the US signals imperial ambitions in the Caribbean once again.

headline: Yeraldine Bonilla — first woman governor in Sinaloa's history
body: After Governor Rocha takes leave following US indictment, Yeraldine Bonilla becomes the first woman to lead Sinaloa. History made amid a political crisis.

headline: Anti-corruption probe hits IPN — 22B peso budget, shell companies exposed
body: Contralinea investigation reveals shell companies and a disputed 5 billion peso Foundation at Mexico's National Polytechnic Institute. The 22 billion peso annual budget under scrutiny.

headline: Cuba marches past the US Embassy on May Day
body: Massive May Day march in Havana passes directly by the US Embassy. Solidarity across Latin America as workers celebrate amid US sanctions and war economy.

headline: Pemex pulls $1B+ in March while feeding its own refineries
body: Pemex generated over $1 billion in revenue in March while simultaneously supplying its own Olmeca and Deer Park refineries. The vertical integration strategy showing results.

headline: Sheinbaum signs salary floor decree — state workers guaranteed $663/day
body: New decree guarantees all federal employees the IMSS average salary of $663/day (+7.1% increase). A concrete policy raising the floor for government workers.

headline: Once-neglected states lead growth — Hidalgo at 4.2% (7x national average)
body: States historically ignored by previous administrations now leading Mexico's economic growth. Hidalgo at 4.2% — seven times the national average. The 4T investment thesis playing out in the data.

headline: NYT: "Sheinbaum's Dilemma: Defy the U.S. or Arrest an Ally"
body: The New York Times frames Mexico's insistence on due process as a "dilemma" — as if sovereignty and rule of law are obstacles rather than principles. Classic false binary: obey Washington or be labeled defiant.

headline: Bloomberg: "Sheinbaum to Announce Steps to Boost Private Investment"
body: Rare positive framing from Bloomberg — actually covering Mexico's proactive economic policy rather than the usual crisis narrative. Steel agreements, Ternium's $8B investment, and industrial sovereignty getting airtime.

headline: Breitbart: "Doubles Down on Protecting Cartel-Connected Ruling Party"
body: Breitbart doing Breitbart things — labeling Mexico's entire ruling party as "cartel-connected" based on a single US indictment with undisclosed evidence. No Mexican sources, no context, pure inflammatory framing.

headline: ICIJ: US gun dealer charged with terrorism for arming cartels
body: Counter-narrative of the week: The International Consortium of Investigative Journalists covers terrorism charges against a US gun dealer who armed cartels. The supply side of violence — the story US media almost never tells.

headline: SILENCE: Hondurasgate leaked audios — zero US coverage
body: Leaked audio revealing a Trump-backed plot in Honduras gets absolutely zero coverage in US mainstream media. When the US is the protagonist of interference, the press looks away.

headline: IMSS: 22.7M formal jobs — all-time record
body: +207K jobs in Q1 2026, +250K over 12 months. Average salary: $663.5/day (+7.1% YoY). The employment machine keeps setting records.

headline: Steel agreement: Ternium invests $8B in Nuevo León
body: Ternium announces $8 billion investment in Pesquería, NL — 3 million tons/year plant, 90K direct jobs. National steel now mandatory in public works. Industrial sovereignty taking shape.

headline: Diesel drops to $27/L — 6-month pact
body: Diesel price falls from ~$28.50 to $27/L under a 6-month agreement. Without the deal, price would be ~$35/L. Includes bank fee reductions on card payments.

headline: Debt: 50.4% of GDP in Q1 2026
body: SHRFSP Q1 2026: 50.4% of GDP (up from 49.8% in Feb). Net federal debt: 46.7% of GDP. Manageable levels but trending up — worth watching.

headline: Insecurity perception falls to 61.5% — lowest in years
body: ENSU March 2026: insecurity perception drops to 61.5% from 63.8% in Dec 2025. Marina best-rated institution at 87.3%. The trend is clear — Mexicans are feeling safer.

headline: Homicides 2025: 77/day in Jan → 52/day in Dec (-32%)
body: SESNSP revised 2025 data shows daily homicides fell from 77.1 in January to 52.4 in December — a 32% decline over the year. Plus: 2,500+ clandestine fentanyl/meth labs dismantled since Oct 2024.

headline: Trade surplus: $5.9B in March — exports up 27.7%
body: Trade balance March 2026: exports $70.7B (+27.7%), imports $64.8B (+24.3%), surplus $5.9B. Mexico is selling more than it buys — the trade engine running hot.

headline: China's consul in Tijuana calls protectionism a dead end
body: China's Consul General Fu Xinrong told a business gathering in Tijuana that unilateralism and protectionism do not benefit anyone, calling it a dead end. Timing: weeks before USMCA review where US wants to restrict Chinese firms in Mexico.

headline: USMCA review will put China's role in Mexico supply chains on trial
body: July 2026 USMCA review shaping up as showdown over Chinese-backed manufacturing in Mexico. Mexico attracted 0.9B FDI in first 3 quarters of 2025. Sheinbaum confirmed APEC China attendance and Mexico hosts APEC 2028.

headline: Mexico Jumps 6 Spots in Global FDI Rankings as China+1 Strategy Pays Off
body: Mexico climbed from 25th to 19th in Kearney's 2026 FDI Confidence Index. Manufacturing exports to the US hit $535B in 2025. Sheinbaum's Plan Mexico aims to push investment to 28% of GDP.

headline: Mexico Joins BRICS 20th Anniversary Media Summit — 15 Nations Building a Multipolar Voice
body: Mexico is among 15 countries participating in the first-ever BRICS Global Media Briefing in May 2026, building a multipolar global communications system.

headline: Trump flies to Beijing to court Xi — while telling Mexico to stay away from China
body: Today, Donald Trump arrived in China for a state visit with Xi Jinping — the first by a US president in nearly a decade. Trade deals, agricultural purchases, and tech agreements are all on the table. Meanwhile, Mexico sits under US pressure to maintain 50% tariffs on Chinese imports, restrict Chinese manufacturing, and tighten USMCA rules of origin — all to contain China.

headline: Mexico ranks #1 in Latin America for Chinese investment by number of operations
body: Despite US pressure and tariffs of up to 50% on Chinese imports, Mexico led all of Latin America in Chinese FDI by transaction count between 2020 and 2025: 98 operations generating 157,338 jobs. Overall Chinese FDI in Latin America fell over 50% in 2025 — but Mexico's position as top destination by number of deals shows productive investment keeps flowing.
